The key concern: the test source code uses stub methods `Connect`, `IsConnected`, `AddChild` that don't actually map to §7 whitelist API names because the canonical name matching relies on `GodotApiWhitelist.All` entries. The test defines `public void Connect(object s, object c)` — but the analyzer matches by invocation canonical name against `GodotApiWhitelist.All`. The canonical of `Connect` is "connect". Is there a "Connect" entry in `GodotApiWhitelist.All`? Yes — `M("Connect", ...)` with GodotApi "Connect". Canonical("Connect") = "connect". So the stub method call `Connect(new object(), new object())` → RawName returns "Connect" (IdentifierNameSyntax) → CanonicalOfInvocation → "connect" → matches whitelist entry "Connect". 

But wait — the test method `Connect` is a user-defined void method, not an actual Godot API. But the analyzer is purely syntactic: it matches on canonical name.
